newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Adelaide City Council to be replaced.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Adelaide City Council to be replaced.

text.p: Legislation to replace the Adelaide City Council with three commissioners, pending elections for a new and restructured council, is to be introduced in South Australia within weeks.
Premier Dean Brown said in a statement on Tuesday the City of Adelaide must again become the focus for South Australia's business, commercial, social, sporting and cultural activities.
"This legislation will help achieve these objectives," he said, adding the commissioners would administer until June 1999.
The State Government action comes as the Adelaide City Council is embroiled in a row over the establishment of investment links with Libya by the Lord Mayor Henry Ninio.
Brown said the council had not adequately reflected the broad interests of key stakeholders in the city, who had suffered from "the gridlock which arises from short-term, factional decision-making".
The state government said in the statement the measures reflected similar directions which had been successfully implemented in Sydney and Melbourne.
